subject: Annual renewal — commit right-sizing & uplift cap discussion
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Wells <anna@cloudwave.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation + draft SOW and tiered pricing

Hi Anna,

Hope you had a good weekend. CloudWave's renewal is coming up on 2026-11-15 and I wanted to share an updated renewal path that reflects your growth over the past 12 months and keeps per-token economics predictable. Attached is a draft SOW with a few commit options — summary below.

High-level proposal (hosted API, usage-based):
- Tier A: 0–50M tokens/month committed — base price $0.0022/token, no volume discount.
- Tier B: 50–200M tokens/month committed — $0.0018/token for tokens in this band (10% effective discount).
- Tier C: >200M tokens/month committed — $0.0014/token for tokens above 200M (additional 22% discount).
- Annual true-up window: 30 days after term end. We propose a renewal uplift cap of 40% on committed monthly tokens (so renewal cannot exceed prior year commit by more than 40% without renegotiation).

Flexibility items:
- One-time right-size (down) permitted mid-term subject to a true-down calculation and a pro-rated fee (details in SOW).
- Optional dedicated capacity pilot for burst-heavy workloads (separate addendum).

Can we schedule a 30-minute sync this week to walk through the SOW and any packaging questions? I copied product and CS for any technical/ops clarifications.

Thanks,
Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Anna Wells <anna@cloudwave.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + draft SOW and tiered pricing

Thanks, Karthik.

Appreciate the detailed SOW. A few quick notes from my side after looking at internal forecasts and the Q3 usage you requested (attached):
- We like the tiered approach but the proposed uplift cap of 40% is a bit high for our finance team. Can we agree to a 25% uplift cap at renewal instead? They want a hard ceiling to limit unexpected spend.
- The one-time right-size down clause: we need clarity on the penalty math (how a true-down is calculated). Our CFO also asked whether any unused committed tokens can roll forward.
- If we move to Tier B/C commits, can you guarantee the per-token price applies to marginal tokens only (not retroactively to the whole volume)?

Looping in our legal (legal@cloudwave.com) to start reviewing the SOW.

Best,
Anna
Anna Wells
Head of Product Ops, CloudWave
anna@cloudwave.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Wells <anna@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + draft SOW and tiered pricing

Anna — thanks for the quick read and the usage file. Couple responses inline and a revised SOW is attached.

- Uplift cap: We can consider lowering the renewal uplift cap to 35% (from 40%) as a concession if CloudWave signs a 12-month commit at Tier B or higher. That trade lets us preserve capacity planning predictability while addressing your finance ask.
- True-down math: the approach we'd run is pro-rated (committed tokens less actual usage), with a 90-day true-up window after term end. For mid-term one-time right-size (down): we can allow a single true-down up to 15% of monthly committed tokens in the contract year (no retroactive rate changes), and any reduction will be pro-rated and credited back as account credit. Details are in Section 4 of the attached SOW.
- Marginal pricing: yes — each tier price applies marginally to tokens in that band. This will be explicit in the pricing table of the SOW.

Other options that might help:
- Roll-forward: we can allow up to 10% of unused committed tokens to be rolled into the next quarter (one-time), but not year-to-year by default.
- Auto-rightsize trigger: we can add an optional check-in mid-year; if sustained usage is 20%+ below committed baseline for 2 consecutive months, we can trigger a review and offer a one-time true-down (subject to the 15% cap).

If that sounds reasonable I can ask Lauren to approve the uplift-cap concession and we can move towards DocuSign. If your legal has redlines, please send them and we'll get Ben on the thread for commercial/legal questions.

Thanks,
Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Anna Wells <anna@cloudwave.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudWave Legal <legal@cloudwave.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + draft SOW and tiered pricing

Karthik — this is moving in the right direction. A couple follow-ups from legal/finance after a quick sync:
- The 35% uplift cap concession is acceptable as long as it is a firm cap (no exceptions). Please confirm in writing.
- The 15% mid-year right-size sounds fair, however our CFO wants an option to reduce commits by up to 25% mid-term if there is a significant downturn, in exchange for an incremental one-time termination fee equal to 10% of the pro-rated remaining commitment. Is Redwood open to that as an alternative path?
- Also: can you confirm whether dedicated capacity pilot pricing would be credited against committed spend if we convert to full reserved capacity within the first 6 months?

If you can get a written internal approval on the uplift cap + clarify the mid-term alternative (25% down with a 10% fee), legal will circulate limited redlines and we can move to signature.

Best,
Anna
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Anna Wells <anna@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + draft SOW and tiered pricing

Hi Anna — thanks for laying out CloudWave's position and the alternative proposal. I reviewed the ask with finance and product.

Short answer: we can approve the following commercial exception for this renewal cycle only (to balance CloudWave's runway concerns and our capacity planning):
- Renewal uplift cap: confirmed at 35% (firm cap).
- Mid-term adjustments: we will allow a one-time mid-term right-size down up to 25% in lieu of the 15% standard true-down, provided CloudWave pays a one-time fee equal to 10% of the pro-rated remainder of committed spend. This exception is a one-time option per contract year and cannot be combined with the standard 15% true-down.
- Dedicated capacity pilot: pilot fees will be credited to committed spend if CloudWave converts to Reserved Capacity within 90 days of pilot completion (not 6 months).

Please confirm acceptance and Lauren will send the final SOW for signature via DocuSign.

Thanks and looking forward to continuing the partnership.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
